title: Waring's problem involving D.H. Lehmer numbers
summary: For every positive integer $a$ which is coprime with $p$, $p$ is an odd prime, we denote by $\overline{a}$ the unique integer satisfying $1\leq \overline{a}\leq p$ and $a\overline{a}\equiv 1(\mathrm{mod}~p)$. Put $$L(p)=\{a\in Z^+:(a,p)=1,2\nmid a+\overline{a}\}.$$ The elements of $L(p)$ are called D.H. Lehmer numbers. The main purpose of this paper is to prove that for any fixed odd prime $p$, every sufficiently large number unless it is congruent to 15 or 16$(\mathrm{mod}~{16})$ is representable as the sum of 14 fourth powers of D.H.
